lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: deriving ASA, SAS, and SSS from rigid motion
lessonRef.title: Discussion or problem seminar: deriving ASA, SAS, and SSS from rigid motion

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One approach is shown. There is at least one other that works.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: For each, name a second method before you solve it.

items.prompt: A rigid motion is a transformation that …
choices: maps every figure to a similar figure
preserves area but may change side lengths
preserves shape but may change size
preserves distance and angle measure

items.prompt: In two triangles, two pairs of corresponding angles and the pair of included sides are congruent. Which congruence criterion applies?
choices: SAS
AAS
ASA
SSS

items.prompt: Two triangles share two pairs of congruent sides and a pair of congruent angles that are not between those sides. Why does this fail to prove congruence?
choices: The angle must be a right angle for any criterion to apply.
Two sides are never enough information under any circumstances.
The triangles are congruent, but the criterion is simply named differently.
The unknown side can close the triangle in two different ways, producing one acute and one obtuse triangle from the same measurements.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Triangle ABC is congruent to triangle DEF. In triangle ABC, ∠A = 37° and ∠B = 75°. Find ∠F.
If a sequence of rigid motions maps △ABC onto △DEF, then …
choices: the triangles have equal area but need not be congruent
every pair of corresponding sides and angles is congruent
only the corresponding angles are congruent
only the corresponding sides are congruent

items.prompt: In two triangles, two pairs of corresponding angles and a pair of non-included sides are congruent. Which congruence criterion applies?
choices: AAS
ASA
SSS
SAS

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Argue for one method over another. Say what makes it better, not just that it is.

items.prompt: Triangle ABC is congruent to triangle DEF. In triangle ABC, ∠A = 67° and ∠B = 46°. Find ∠F.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Triangle ABC is congruent to triangle DEF. In triangle ABC, ∠A = 53° and ∠B = 27°. Find ∠F.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
